transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-10-21
Time: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Tom Alvarez (Product), Lena Ortiz (Redwood Partnerships); Marta Ruiz (Velos CTO), Evan Li (Velos Platform Eng), Sofia Khan (Velos Partner PM), Daniel Brooks (Velos Security)

Summary:
Brief sync to align on joint solution reference architecture, marketplace listing requirements, go-to-market assets, and a plan for a perf/security POC. High-level agreement on responsibilities and next steps.

Topics:
- Reference architecture for Redwood runtime on Velos marketplace offering
- Marketplace integration checklist (listing metadata, billing, support contact)
- Security and compliance (KMS, audit logs, SSO/SAML, data residency)
- Technical runbook for deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private/VPC)
- Joint benchmarking plan and success criteria

Action items (captured above).

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, uh good morning, thanks for joining. I think we have about, what did we say, 50 minutes? 52? so we can run through the RA, checklist and security.
[00:09] Marta Ruiz: Morning Alex, thanks - excited to get this scoped. We are primarily interested in a joint marketplace offering that we can list in the Velos marketplace and link to Redwood dedicated or private options.
[00:18] Alex Chen: Yep, and we want to make sure the listing supports both hosted and Velos-managed private deployments, right? Lena will walk through partnership requirements later.
[00:30] Lena Ortiz: hi all, quick note - marketplace metadata we need: logos, short/long descriptions, technical tags (vpc, sso, dedicated-gpu), support contacts, and a billing integration overview.
[00:40] Sofia Khan: quick Q - billing integration, we usually require a metered billing hook. Do you support marketplace billing APIs or will it be via reseller invoicing?
[00:50] Tom Alvarez: For Redwood hosted we can integrate with marketplace metering APIs - for dedicated/private we typically do contract/reseller billing. There is some nuance around usage reporting and attribution.
[01:02] Evan Li: On the technical side we need to understand network topology for private deployments, specifically whether Redwood requires inbound access or we can do peering. Also curious about KV cache persistence and how that fits into our infra.
[01:18] Priya Patel: Good question. For private/VPC we support VPC peering and customer-managed networking; the control plane can either be hosted or run in a customer-managed plane depending on enterprise needs. The KV cache is in-memory on the inference nodes - we do optional warmup snapshots but nothing persisted to customer S3 by default unless you enable caching export.
[01:36] Daniel Brooks: that's helpful, can you outline encryption at rest and KMS integration? We need to map to our HSM/KMS standards.
[01:44] Priya Patel: Sure, we integrate with customer KMS for private deployments - we can support both cloud KMS and HSM-backed keys. For hosted we use Redwood's defaults but offer customer-managed KMS for enterprise accounts. Audit logs are exportable for all modes.
[01:59] Marta Ruiz: Any gotchas with SSO? We run Okta and need SAML/SCIM provisioning.
[02:06] Alex Chen: SAML and SCIM are in our enterprise offering; we can provide an IdP integration guide. We should schedule a security-specific deep dive with your security team to go through claim mappings.
[02:18] Daniel Brooks: yes please, I'll collect questions. Also curious about token-level auditing - can you provide per-request logs with trace ids?
[02:27] Priya Patel: We surface trace ids in our logs and the console can map request tokens, timestamps, latencies, and token counts per call. Retention windows vary by plan but we can provide extended retention as an add-on.
[02:39] Sofia Khan: On the RA - what does the recommended topology look like if we want a Velos-managed private deployment, with Redwood runtime colocated in Velos tenant?
[02:49] Tom Alvarez: Typically the reference arch we propose: customer (Velos) VPC with dedicated GPU nodes running Redwood inference runtime, a small control-plane connector that talks to Redwood control plane over TLS (optional to run fully air-gapped), and an ingress balancer managed by Velos. We document certs, ports, and peering instructions in the RA.
[03:05] Marta Ruiz: ok, and the latency SLOs - what are reasonable expectations? We're targeting sub-150ms for small prompts and ~300-500ms for 1k token responses - is that realistic on dedicated GPUs?
[03:20] Priya Patel: For dedicated GPU pools and good network topology sub-150ms is achievable for short prompts on models similar to redwood-5b style, but it depends on model choice, sequence length, quantization, and batching. For larger responses expect higher tail latencies. We'll capture expected perf numbers in the benchmark plan.
[03:38] Evan Li: Speaking of models, will the marketplace listing allow customers to select model variants? e.g., quantized vs fp16?
[03:45] Alex Chen: Yes, the listing metadata can enumerate supported model variants and recommended defaults. We also recommend a compatibility matrix showing the tradeoffs (latency vs cost).
[03:54] Marta Ruiz: go-to-market - who publishes the listing assets? We want co-branded pages and a joint datasheet.
[04:00] Lena Ortiz: We'll provide a co-branding pack; Velos provides logos and customer-facing copy. Redwood will draft the technical datasheet and run it by your PM for approval.
[04:09] Sofia Khan: On legal - do we need a separate reseller agreement or is this a standard marketplace terms?
[04:15] Alex Chen: Typically marketplace listing uses Velos marketplace terms for purchases but for dedicated/private there is a separate contract. Legal will coordinate. We can share a checklist.
[04:24] Marta Ruiz: Perf benchmarking - what data do you need from us to run the POC?
[04:29] Priya Patel: Sample prompts and expected concurrency, representative payload sizes, and a dev cluster where we can run controlled tests. Also, network latency between Redwood test agents and your environment if we do hosted-to-velos runs.
[04:40] Evan Li: We can provide a small dev cluster with 2 x A100 equiv and sample dataset. We'll also share expected QPS and concurrency profile.
[04:48] Priya Patel: Perfect. We'll run a baseline with default batching and then test optimized batching/kv-caching. We'll produce latency percentiles, token throughput, and cost estimate per 1M tokens.
[04:59] Daniel Brooks: On the security deep dive - do you have SOC2/ISO artifacts and a pen test report?
[05:05] Alex Chen: We have SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 - can share an NDA'd package. For pen tests we have vendor reports; we'll surface redacted summaries and remediation items.
[05:15] Marta Ruiz: Great. A few clarifying points on the RA doc - can you include a section for rollback/fallback? e.g., if our dedicated pool is saturated, can requests be routed to Redwood hosted as fallback?
[05:27] Tom Alvarez: Yes, smart routing and fallback are part of the runtime. We can configure routing policies: prefer private, fallback to hosted or to a smaller model variant. We'll document constraints and how to configure the routing rules in the RA.
[05:40] Sofia Khan: For the marketplace listing flow, what is required for the first pass? We want to get a beta listing up in a month.
[05:48] Lena Ortiz: First pass needs: short/long description, 3 screenshots, pricing model outline, support contact, and an initial reference architecture summary. For a beta we can publish with a link to an onboarding doc and mark it as early access.
[06:01] Marta Ruiz: Are there any pre-reqs for security review? Our procurement requires proof of encryption, SSO, and incident response.
[06:09] Daniel Brooks: yes, and also data residency options; some customers will ask data not to leave EU.
[06:16] Priya Patel: We support region pinning for dedicated/private; hosted also offers region controls in selected regions. We'll include data residency options in the RA and marketplace metadata.
[06:26] Evan Li: One technical nit - how do you handle model updates and rollouts in dedicated pools? We can't have sudden regressions.
[06:34] Tom Alvarez: Rollouts are gradual: canary deploys, can route a small percentage of traffic for validation, and automatic fallback if error rates regress. We also support pinned model versions per route so you can opt into upgrades.
[06:47] Marta Ruiz: that answers it. Another question: what level of support response times do you guarantee for marketplace customers vs enterprise customers?
[06:56] Alex Chen: Marketplace customers get standard support SLAs (48-72 hour responses); Dedicated contract customers get enterprise SLAs including on-call and faster response times. We'll put the exact tiers in the listing.
[07:06] Sofia Khan: On the integration checklist, can you enumerate the technical docs we should expect?
[07:12] Alex Chen: Sure - RA PDF, deployment runbook, SSO guide, KMS integration guide, traffic routing and firewall rules, benchmark guide, and a quickstart with sample terraform snippets.
[07:21] Evan Li: terraform snippets are big for us - can you provide templates for peering, IAM roles, and node pool configs?
[07:27] Priya Patel: Yes, we'll provide tf modules and helm charts for customers choosing the private deployment path.
[07:34] Marta Ruiz: OK, sounds good. Let's talk timelines - if we aim to publish a beta marketplace listing in 4 weeks, what does Redwood need this week?
[07:43] Alex Chen: This week we need logos, a short description, and your target pricing model. We'll draft the RA and checklist and get it to you by next week.
[07:54] Sofia Khan: Pricing - will you publish recommended pricing or will Velos set pricing?
[07:59] Lena Ortiz: For co-listing we typically provide a recommended retail price and discounting tiers; Velos can set the final price in the marketplace.
[08:07] Marta Ruiz: Any integration pieces that tend to block a marketplace listing?
[08:11] Tom Alvarez: Network certs and billing integration are the two most common blockers. Also missing support contact or legal terms.
[08:20] Daniel Brooks: I'll start collecting the security checklist items and share them. Also we might ask for a short architecture review with our security team - next week would be ideal.
[08:30] Alex Chen: Great - let's pencil in a security deep dive next Tuesday 10am PT. We'll invite Priya and Tom.
[08:36] Marta Ruiz: Tuesday works.
[08:39] Priya Patel: quick technical question for Evan - when you said A100-equivalent nodes, are you able to give the baseline GPU/CPU RAM and network attach? It helps us recommend model variants.
[08:50] Evan Li: yes, 2 x A100 40GB, 512GB RAM, 100Gbps network. We can provide exact specs in a doc.
[08:58] Priya Patel: perfect. We'll run a baseline for the recommended models and quantization profiles.
[09:05] Sofia Khan: Marketing - who owns the co-branded datasheet?
[09:09] Lena Ortiz: Redwood will draft and Velos will review. We'll coordinate with your marketing lead.
[09:15] Marta Ruiz: ok. Anything else on go-to-market?
[09:19] Alex Chen: We'll also propose a webinar and joint blog post once the beta listing is live.
[09:25] Marta Ruiz: good.
[09:28] Tom Alvarez: one more technical point - for the perf benchmark we should outline success criteria: p50/p95 latency targets, throughput targets at target concurrency, and cost per 1M tokens. Also check stability under sustained load.
[09:40] Priya Patel: agreed, we'll include a benchmarking template.
[09:44] Evan Li: We'll provide test user accounts and a dev cluster.
[09:48] Alex Chen: ok, let's recap next steps quickly.
[09:51] Alex Chen: Redwood: circulate RA draft, marketplace checklist, tf snippets, and benchmark template by next Wed (2026-10-28).
[09:59] Alex Chen: Velos: provide logos, short description, pricing intent, network/topology details by 2026-10-25.
[10:07] Alex Chen: Security deep dive scheduled for Tue next week 10am PT.
[10:12] Marta Ruiz: confirmed.
[10:14] Daniel Brooks: I'll send the initial security questions compendium.
[10:17] Alex Chen: Great - thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites and the doc links.
[10:21] Marta Ruiz: thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
